crs_reference.name: Korean 1985 / Modified Central Belt
crs_reference.important_distinction: EPSG formal axis labels do not by themselves prove how the upstream CSV fields named coordinate X/Y are populated

probe_method.candidate_a: interpret source 좌표정보(X) as easting and 좌표정보(Y) as northing, then transform EPSG:5174 to EPSG:4326 with always_xy=true
probe_method.candidate_b: interpret source 좌표정보(X) as northing and 좌표정보(Y) as easting by swapping values before the same transform
probe_method.macro_region_heuristic: compare transformed coordinates with coarse WGS84 envelopes derived only from first-level Korean administrative address prefixes; no row-level addresses or coordinates are retained
probe_method.strong_preference_rule: at least 100 macro-region-eligible pairs, preferred match rate at least 90%, and margin over the other candidate at least 40 percentage points

limitations: the first 5000 nonblank coordinate pairs per source are deterministic but not a nationwide stratified sample
both candidate axis interpretations fall inside a broad Korea envelope for all sampled pairs, so broad geographic plausibility alone cannot distinguish them
the decisive comparison uses coarse first-level-address macro-region envelopes and is a QA heuristic rather than authoritative geocoding
formal EPSG axis labels and upstream CSV X/Y field naming are distinct concepts
no WGS84 row-level columns are approved until a stronger full-spread or full-snapshot axis QA gate passes
next_gate: user executes the deterministic full-snapshot aggregate-only coordinate-axis validation before setting coordinate_axis_order_validated=true or generating WGS84 columns
